description: Ex-USAF 47-0205, c/n 080-1966; served FAU 1958-1970s. Restored 2014 for the new hangar; photographed inside the hangar 2016 and listed on the museum's aircraft page (archived January 2026).

Ex-USAF 55-4443 (c/n 580-9887); some sources describe it as an AT-33A. Photographed at the museum July 2016; museum list gives a single T-33A so 203 and 205 may not both still be on the museum site - see notes.
aliases: T33A; AT-33A; AT33A; 55-4443; 203; Silver Star; T33

description: Displayed outdoors on the museum apron; Aerial Visuals gives ex-USAF 53-5860 (AT-33A). Photographed on its outdoor plinth December 2016; the Wikipedia article (2026) lists FAU 205 among the restored outdoor exhibits.
Ex-USAF 69-6429, c/n 43276; delivered to the museum 4 December 2007 and displayed in the hangar (photographed 2016, listed 2018 and on the museum page archived January 2026).
Ex-Argentine Air Force A-547, delivered to Uruguay 23 September 1981; retired 2017 and displayed in the museum hangar (photographed 2016 and listed 2018).
aliases: IA58 Pucará; IA-58A; IA58A; A-547; 224; A547

description: Ex-Brazilian Air Force 5087; sources conflict on its USAAF serial (44-30743 per Aerial Visuals c/n 108-34017; 43-27847 per a 2009 survey). Restored and displayed in the hangar as FAU 156 'Charrúa'; earlier wore G3-158 and G3-160.
Ex-USAAF 42-37235, c/n 3738; in FAU service 1947-1980. Photographed at the museum 2017 and listed 2018 (outdoor in 2018, hangar list 2026).
Displayed in the hangar; photographed 2016 and listed on the museum page (2026). A 2009 survey recorded it as ex-USAF 51-14775 - unverified.

Airworthy heritage aircraft of the museum/FAU (civil registration CX-NAT), flown from Brigada Aérea I; solo flights recorded December 2023 and July 2025. Hangared with the flying squadron rather than in the museum hall - seen at open days.

Curtiss-Wright CW-22 built as an SNC-1 for the US Navy; FAU trainer from 1942, marked E-205 (also recorded as G2-205). Fuselage repaired by the AAMA 2008; displayed in the hangar (photographed 2016-2018).
Marked E-620; photographed in the hangar July 2016 and on the museum list 2026. A 2009 survey called it a PT-19B ex-634/675 - identity not confirmed.
Ex-US Navy T-34B, c/n BG-222; photographed at El Jagüel in 1996 and later at the museum (2016). On the museum list 2026.

Chipmunk wearing civil registration CX-AVA, restored by the museum (photographed 2016; 'restoration in progress' 2018). Possibly the ex-FAU Chipmunk restored as 'Urutau' - first of two Chipmunks in the collection.
Chipmunk c/n C1/0969 retaining British registration G-ANOW; photographed in the hangar July 2016 and recorded in 2009. Second of two Chipmunks in the collection.
aliases: DHC1; Chipmunk 22; C1/0969; second of two

description: Piper J-5C/AE-1 air ambulance, c/n 5-1443; served the FAU as S-503 and later flew as CX-AEU. Displayed as S-503 (photographed 2016, listed 2018 and 2026).
aliases: AE1; J-5C; J5C; HE-1; CX-AEU; 503; HE1

description: First aircraft restored by the Asociación Amigos del Museo; displayed in the hangar (2016-2026).
Ryan NA-145 Navion c/n NAV-4-1118, painted as FAU '1903' (the Navion flew with the FAU); fitted with a flight-simulator display. Photographed 2016, listed 2018 and 2026.
Glider displayed in the hangar; photographed 2016 and listed 2018 and 2026.
EMB-110C, the first Brazilian-built aircraft ever exported (1975); retired 2014 and displayed inside the main hangar (photographed 2016, listed 2026).
Displayed in the hangar (listed 2018 and 2026).
In FAU service 1965-2000; displayed in the hangar (listed 2018 and 2026).
Uruguayan Navy Tracker, ex-BuNo 152376, c/n 263C, ex-VS-37 USS Hornet; transferred to Uruguay January 1981, moved from Laguna del Sauce to the museum 2018. Photographed on display June 2019.
Ex-US Army UH-1B (c/n 283); in FAU service 1975-1990. Displayed in the hangar (photographed 2016, listed 2026).
Bell UH-1H c/n 13210 (built 1973), restored and repainted by the AAMA 2008; photographed in the hangar July 2016.

Ex-RAF Wessex HC.2, c/n WA122 (built 1963), acquired by the FAU 1997; displayed in the hangar with rotor blades folded (photographed July 2016, listed 2026). Not to be confused with FAU 071 now at Cardona.
Ex-German Army Bo 105P (PAH-1) operated by the FAU; displayed in the hangar (listed 2026). Serial not readable in available photographs.
Hiller UH-12E-4/OH-23F c/n 2297; flew with the FAU (reported as 026) and later as CX-BNR. Displayed in the hangar (listed 2009, 2026).

C-47B-35-DK 44-77060 (c/n 16644/33392), ex-RAF KN682/XF767, G-AMNL, I-TAVO; flew for PLUNA as CX-BDB. Restored in PLUNA colours 2014 and displayed outdoors beside the hangar with a memorial to the 1962 CX-AGE accident (photographed 2016; Memorias de PLUNA events 2021-2025).
aliases: DC3; C-47B; C47B; 44-77060; KN682; XF767; G-AMNL; I-TAVO

description: Cockpit/forward fuselage section only, displayed in the hangar as FAU T-521; Wikipedia's C-47 survivors list gives it as ex-USAAF 42-100768. Listed on the museum page 2026.

400th Viscount built; first flight 6 December 1958, ex-VASP PP-SRF, PLUNA 1976-1982. Moved to the museum site 2017; interior restored by Memorias de PLUNA from 2021 and opened to visitors on scheduled days (2024-2026); exterior still awaits repaint.
Lockheed 18-56 c/n 18-2349, ex-USAAF 42-32215, seized in a cigarette-smuggling case at Florida (Uruguay); stored outdoors at the museum awaiting restoration (photographed 1993, 2018).
Aero Commander 680 (U-4B type) of the FAU photographic squadron; displayed outdoors, photographed December 2016 and named among the restored outdoor exhibits (Wikipedia 2026).
Restored by the Asociación Amigos del Museo and formally handed over 31 August 2022; listed on the museum aircraft page 2026. Identity not marked in available sources.
Uruguayan-designed light aircraft (1947); burnt in the 1997 museum fire, the surviving metal structure was restored by the AAMA and is exhibited (2022).
Reproduction of the 1915 Castaibert VI (70 hp) built by Pablo Castaibert in Buenos Aires; the museum presents it as the only example in the world. Replica, not an original airframe.
Reproduction of the 1910 Blériot XI displayed in the hangar (museum list 2026). Replica, not an original airframe.
Reproduction Farman biplane with rotary engine representing Uruguay's first military school aircraft; displayed in the hangar. Replica, not an original airframe.
